transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because lately my head just keeps jumping around. On the road I’ll notice every CB call, every fuel sign, some random idea, and then I miss things I shouldn’t—delivery notes, calls I said I’d return. It’s been going on a while, and it’s starting to cause problems.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying focused?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big issue back then… school was school, you know. I got through it.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or keyed up compared with your normal self?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll get kind of keyed up and start finding extra things to do—messing with route plans, checking in on newer drivers after hours, fixing stuff at home. Sitting still too long makes me feel antsy.
When you get keyed up like that, do you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah… I guess so. Most nights I’m only getting maybe three or four hours, then I’m up before daylight and feel ready to go, not really tired.
During those times when you sleep only three or four hours, do you also feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah… sometimes I feel really up, like everything’s gonna work out no matter what. But other times it’s more like I’m just fired up and snapping over little things, especially at home. It’s been like that for months, I guess.
Do these times when you sleep only three or four hours happen in distinct stretches, rather than being your usual pattern all the time?
I don’t know if I’d call it stretches exactly… it’s been most nights lately. I’ll sleep maybe three or four hours, then I’m up before daylight feeling ready to roll, not really worn out.
Was there a time when needing only three or four hours of sleep felt like a clear change from how you usually are?
Yeah… I mean, I used to sleep more than that. Lately it’s been most nights, three or four hours, and then I’m up before daylight feeling like I can get going, not really worn out.
During these times, have you been spending much more money than usual?
Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, I buy stuff here and there, but… I don’t think it’s been way more than usual.
Before these past few months, had you ever had another separate period like this when you needed much less sleep and still felt full of energy?

Not really sure. I mean… right now it’s been most nights, sleeping three or four hours and still getting up before daylight ready to go. Before that, I don’t know if there was a separate time like this.
When you’re in those keyed-up periods, do you find yourself talking much more than usual?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really paid attention to that. I don’t think I’m running my mouth nonstop or anything.
During this keyed-up time, have these symptoms caused serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah… some. I don’t know if I’d call it serious, but it’s caused problems.

At work, I’ve had dispatch and clients having to repeat things I should’ve caught the first time. And a couple sales follow-ups slipped by because I was trying to chase too many things at once.

At home… my wife and daughter seem like they’re kind of walking on eggshells around me. I can tell I’m adding strain when I’m supposed to be helping.
When you sleep only three or four hours, do you still feel rested?
Yeah… mostly. Even if it’s only three or four hours, I’m up before daylight feeling like I can get going, not really worn out.
Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with bipolar disorder?
Not that I know of. My family didn’t really talk about that kind of stuff much, so… I can’t say for sure.
Lately, have you been taking on a lot more projects or activities than is normal for you?
Yeah… I guess so. I keep giving myself extra stuff to do — messing with route plans, checking in on newer drivers after hours, little repairs around the house. If I sit too long, I get kind of antsy.
During these keyed-up times, do you feel more confident or capable than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I do. I got thinking I could redo the whole driver training thing myself, make it run better than the bosses have it. Which… probably isn’t really my place, but at the time it felt like I could handle it.
When you’re feeling keyed up, do your thoughts race?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say they race, exactly. I just get a lot on my mind and it’s hard to settle it down sometimes.
Have there been times when you felt unusually irritable compared with your normal self?

Yeah… more than usual, I’d say. For a few months I’ve been kind of… either really fired up, like everything’s gonna work out, or I’m snapping over little things at home, out in the yard. That’s not really how I usually am.
Before these past few months, were problems with attention and distractibility something you had regularly since childhood?

No… not really since childhood. I mean, I got through school fine enough. This is more recent. Lately my attention just jumps—CB goes off, a fuel price sign, some new idea—and then I miss stupid details I normally wouldn’t, like a delivery note or who I was supposed to call back.
